title: Introduction to Python

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
Python is used for automation, web services, and data analysis because its readable syntax and broad library ecosystem make small, testable steps practical.
CORE EXPLANATION

Python is a readable, general-purpose programming language used for automation, web services, data processing, scientific computing, and education. Dynamic typing and a broad standard library support rapid prototyping; performance, mobile, and real-time constraints still need separate evaluation.

HISTORY, CREATOR, AND MOTIVATION

Python was created by Guido van Rossum: work began in December 1989, and the first public release, 0.9.0, appeared in February 1991. The name refers to the Monty Python comedy group, not the snake. The goal was a readable, general-purpose language. Python is now used for web services, test automation, data analysis, scientific computing, and DevOps. The official Python success stories include examples from organizations such as Philips, D-Link Australia, and AstraZeneca; each chose Python for different work. This does not mean Python is the only technology they use: teams choose tools for each project. Source: https://www.python.org/about/success/
